evidence/reviews/faa-wildlife-strike-sub.method: 2000 paired whole-entity draws, pointwise percentile95%; conditional on fitted models, cohort and declared dependence

evidence/reviews/faa-wildlife-strike-sub.reason: Each row is one consolidated FAA strike record, but unique index_nr does not make rows independent. The physically meaningful dependence units are the airport-day (same flock, migration pulse or local conditions; multiple reports or records of one event) and the airframe; the release drops AIRPORT_ID, REG, FLT and OPID, so the finest released key that nests airport-day is (incident_date, state). Training data support it: 135 groups (292 rows) are identical on incident_date and all 18 features under different index_nr, 22 of them with near-adjacent IDs, and their labels are concordant in every group (133 all-negative, 2 all-positive, 0 mixed), which independence at those rows' 1.4% positive rate would make very unlikely; and same-(incident_date, state) positive-positive pairs number 42 against stratified permutation null means of 30.7 to 33.3 (sd 5.3 to 5.9, one-sided p 0.02 to 0.08), while incident_date alone shows no excess (589 observed vs 588 expected). Every exact-duplicate group shares date and state, so the key nests them. Both columns are present in every split file with an identical header; incident_date is a non-predictor carry in the baseline runner and state is a declared feature. The key is a function of incident_date, so no cluster crosses the chronological split boundaries. Chosen from source meaning and train.csv only, before any holdout scoring.
limitations: State-day is a coarser superset of the true airport-day unit; AIRPORT_ID is not in the release, so unrelated strikes at different airports in one state on one day are grouped together (conservative).
Repeated strikes on the same airframe, flight or operator on different days or in different states are not captured, because REG, FLT and OPID are dropped from the release.

Era-level dependence from a shared adjudication regime (positive rate falls from about 2% in 2014 to about 0.4% from 2017) is not captured; a year-level key would leave only four holdout clusters and is unusable.

Evidence of within-cluster label dependence in training is modest (about 10 excess positive pairs out of 2,851 positives, plus 0.35% exact-duplicate rows); the key guards against understated uncertainty rather than correcting a large effect.

Clusters are mostly small: 57% of train rows and 42.5% of public-validation rows (label-free count) are singleton clusters, maximum sizes 16 and 31, so cluster-level resampling will be close to row-level resampling.

Holdout cluster structure was not inspected; no holdout rows or holdout metrics were read. The holdout row count and positive rate published in extract/meta.json were seen as part of the pinned public metadata and did not inform this choice.
